Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. The instructions for joining the question queue will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Robert Kline, Chief Medical Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures; strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year; overview of key financial performance highlights; same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year; capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion; and revenue per admission trends and drivers.

Let me begin with the status of our ongoing and planned acquisitions and divestitures, which remain a cornerstone of our capital allocation strategy at Apex Health Partners. We're navigating a dynamic M&A landscape in the hospitals and healthcare services sector, with accelerating consolidation—deal volume in acute care and outpatient facilities up about 18% year-over-year according to Bain & Company's latest Healthcare M&A report—driven by margin pressures from labor inflation averaging 6-8% across the industry, payer mix shifts toward Medicare Advantage penetration now at 52% nationally, and the need to scale for value-based care under models like the Medicare Shared Savings Program.

Our active pipeline starts with our largest ongoing transaction, the $850 million acquisition of Tri-State Regional Hospitals, a three-facility system with 650 licensed beds in the high-growth Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. Announced in Q2, this deal is on track for closure in early Q1 next year, pending final Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust clearance and state certificate-of-need approvals from the Texas Department of State Health Services. We priced it at an attractive 9.2x trailing twelve-month EBITDA multiple—below the peer median of 11.5x for similar urban acute care assets, per PitchBook data—reflecting seller motivation amid rising interest rates. Post-close, we anticipate $45 million in annual run-rate synergies by Year 2, phased as 40% from procurement optimization via our Group Purchasing Organization leveraging Vizient contracts, 30% from clinical standardization including Epic Hyperspace EHR integration for full interoperability with our existing 85-hospital footprint, and the balance from revenue cycle management enhancements targeting a 200 basis point improvement in cash collections. Strategically, this strengthens our Sunbelt expansion, targeting 15-20% CAGR in adjusted admissions driven by Texas's 1.8 million net migrants since 2020 per U.S. Census data, and positions us to gain share in high-acuity services like neurointerventional suites amid rising stroke volumes.

Complementing this, we're in late-stage diligence on two tuck-in acquisitions totaling $275 million: a 120-bed community hospital in Phoenix, Arizona, and a portfolio of five freestanding emergency departments in the Atlanta suburbs from a divesting Tenet Healthcare affiliate. The Phoenix asset, at 8.5x EBITDA, adds critical mass to our 12-hospital Arizona cluster, improving payer negotiations with players like Banner Health and UnitedHealthcare—our Medicare Advantage mix there currently yields 2-3% better reimbursements than national averages. The ER portfolio supports our outpatient shift strategy; freestanding EDs now account for 22% of our non-acute revenue, up from 14% two years ago, delivering 12% EBITDA margins versus 7% for inpatient and helping mitigate site-neutral payment headwinds from the No Surprises Act. Both deals are expected to close by year-end, adding $30 million to FY'25 EBITDA accretion.

On divestitures, we're disciplined about portfolio optimization. Earlier this quarter, we completed the $120 million sale of our two underperforming skilled nursing facilities in rural upstate New York to a regional long-term care operator. Acquired in our 2021 consolidation play, these had negative 2% EBITDA margins due to staffing ratios—nursing vacancy rates at 25% there versus our system-wide 11%—and a 65% unfavorable Medicaid payer mix. The net proceeds, after $15 million in transaction costs, were redeployed into a $100 million investment in ambulatory surgery centers via a joint venture with United Surgical Partners International. This reduces our rural exposure from 18% to 12% of total beds, sharpening focus on urban and suburban markets where case mix index averages 1.85, 15% above rural peers.

Looking ahead, our M&A pipeline exceeds $2.5 billion in targeted opportunities, screened via our proprietary model for assets with over 10% EBITDA margins, digital health adjacencies like telehealth-enabled platforms similar to Teladoc integrations, and geographic fit with our core Southeast and Southwest markets. We're excited about behavioral health tuck-ins—discussions for a $400 million network of 15 inpatient psych facilities in Florida at a 10x multiple—to address the 25% post-COVID demand surge per CMS data and diversify beyond traditional acute care, which is 68% of our revenue. We're also eyeing physician group roll-ups, akin to Optum's approach, for vertical integration of primary care and upstream referrals amid 4% YoY industry-wide inpatient utilization decline.

Our regional strategy emphasizes growth in population-boom states like Florida and Texas, where bed supply lags demand by 10-12% per AHA metrics, balanced by selective exits in high-cost, low-growth Northeast and Midwest areas. This M&A supports FY'24 guidance of 5-7% revenue growth and 150 basis points margin expansion, with $200 million in synergies embedded. These transactions remain subject to customary closing conditions, regulatory approvals, and market dynamics.

Next, our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year. As a leading operator of acute care hospitals and outpatient facilities across 15 states, Apex Health Partners is tackling a dynamic landscape with robust demand from an aging population, procedural volume recovery, and headwinds like labor inflation and payer mix shifts. Our Q3 results—$2.8 billion in revenue up 7% year-over-year, adjusted EBITDA of $420 million at 15% margin—highlight our model's resilience and set us up for growth.

Our top priorities center on same-facility growth, margin expansion, and value creation amid shifts to site-neutral payments and value-based care.

First, accelerating capacity expansion and market share in high-growth regions. We're pursuing organic and tuck-in growth in Sunbelt markets fueled by demographics and migration. In Q4, we'll add 350 net new licensed beds via three greenfield projects in Texas and Florida—echoing peers like HCA and Tenet, where Sunbelt utilization is 75-80%. Our new 200-bed Dallas-Fort Worth facility, joint ventured with an orthopedic group, targets cardiology and neurosurgery, with case mix index up 2.5 points year-to-date. Southeast admissions in Florida and Georgia grew 5% YoY in Q3, beating national averages on elective orthopedics and oncology at 95% pre-COVID levels. We're cautious in high-regulation states like California and New York; Pacific growth was 2% due to rate issues. For FY2025, $1.2 billion in capex includes two $400-500 million hospital acquisitions and de novo builds for payer volumes from UnitedHealth and Humana.

Second, operational excellence and margin discipline. Q3's 150 basis point expansion to 15% stems from cost control, including 10% drop in contract labor via our CareForce retention program—RN turnover at 12% below 18% benchmark per NSI Nursing Solutions—and 8-10% supply discounts via HealthTrust GPO. Q4 leverage includes ALOS down to 4.5 days via case management and tools. Outpatient ASCs and HOPDs are 42% of revenue, up from 38%, with 12% same-site growth; we're converting 15% HOPD to freestanding ASCs ahead of 2025 Medicare adjustments.

Third, digital transformation and value-based care. Epic MyChart covers 85%, boosting portal use 25% and cutting no-shows 15%. Q4 pilots AI revenue cycle from Change Healthcare for 200 bps A/R improvement (now 45 days) and 98% collections. Value-based covers 35% of lives, up from 28%; MA at 42%, with $45 million YTD shared savings via Elevance on bundles and RPM using Biofourmis—CHF readmissions down 18%. FY2025 doubles MA revenue to $1.5 billion on 10 million enrollee switches per CMS, with CDI for star ratings.

Fourth, workforce optimization and ESG. Amid 15% RN vacancies per AACN, FY2025's $150 million invests in apprenticeships for 2,000 hires and LeanTaaS AI scheduling cutting overtime 20%. ESG hits 50% renewables by year-end with NextEra, cutting costs and appealing to investors.

For outlook: Q4 revenue $2.85-2.95 billion (6-8% growth) from 3-4% same-facility admissions, 2% patient days, 5% RPA on CMI/MA; EBITDA $430-460 million (15-15.5%). FY2025 revenue 7-9%, EBITDA up 12-15% at 15.5-16.5%, EPS $5.80-6.20 with $300 million repurchases. Risks: MA denials up 5%, cyber threats ($50 million allocated); upsides: procedural normalization, M&A.

These priorities position us for above-market growth like HCA's 10% CAGR, with $1 billion share authorization.

Turning to an overview of key financial performance highlights. Good morning again—our Q3 delivered total net revenues of $2.8 billion, up 7% year-over-year, our ninth straight quarter of expansion. This reflects strength in our 52-hospital Sunbelt-focused footprint and pivot to high-margin outpatient/procedural volumes.

Same-facility net patient revenues grew 6.8% on 4.5% admissions to 142,000 from elective orthopedics, cardiology, oncology rebound. Patient days up 3.2% to 785,000, ALOS stable at 5.5 days. CMI up 2.1% to 1.92 on neurovascular, transplants; RPA up 4.3% to $24,800.

Outpatient revenues surged 12% to $1.2 billion (29% total), from 28 ASCs with 15% procedures (joints, cataracts) like HCA/Surgery Partners trends; freestanding EDs up 22%.

Adjusted EBITDA $420 million, up 9.5%, margin 15% (150 bps expansion). Propelled by revenue cycle: 98.2% collections via AI denial tool with Epic. Net income $210 million, $0.92 diluted EPS.

Labor (52% revenues) up 5.8% but moderated via retention—travel nurses 8% vs 12%; AMN contracts amid 4% vacancy per NSI. Supplies up 6.2% on biologics like Keytruda, offset by $45 million GPO savings. Bad debt 3.1%.

Cash flow $550 million (83% EBITDA conversion), $200 million repurchases under $1.5 billion program. Net debt $7.5 billion, 2.9x leverage, $1.8 billion liquidity. Closed $450 million DFW tuck-in, $0.15 EPS accretive.

Sunbelt drove 65% growth: Florida/Texas admissions +7% on 1.2 million migrants, 58% commercial. Midwest/Northeast softer (-1%) on 42% Medicaid, 2.9% IPPS cut; offset by bariatrics/behavioral +18%.

Results validate 'High-Growth, High-Acuity': $150 million YTD capex on da Vinci at 85% facilities (+300 bps ortho), telehealth 25% visits. Value-based pilots with UnitedHealthcare/Blue Cross target 15% risk revenues by 2025. Raising FY revenue to $11.2-11.5 billion, EBITDA $1.65-1.75 billion.

Now, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for next quarter/year. For Q3 context, same-facility excludes tuck-ins like Southeast JV, focusing on 180 core facilities in 22 states.

Q4 same-facility admissions 2.5-3.5% (on Q3 3.1%), from elective ortho/cardio/surgery 8-10% above pre-pandemic like HCA/Tenet. Outpatient 4-5%, ASC/imaging +12%; patient days 2.8-3.8%, CMI 1.72-1.75. FY admissions raised to 3-4%, outpatient 4.5-5.5%, high end on Sunbelt (65% beds).

Q4 revenue 6-7.5%, RPA +3.5-4.5%; commercial index +4.2%, mix 48% commercial/42% Medicare. Outpatient per visit +5-6% on robotics (150 da Vinci). FY revenue 7-8.5% ($1.2 billion incremental), +150 bps value-based (25% Medicare lives).

Sunbelt (FL/TX/AZ) 5%+ volumes; Florida 6.2% Q3 per Definitive. Northeast/Midwest mitigated by scheduling. Underpinnings: staffing (turnover 12%, AMN flex, 28.5 admits/FTE); Epic MyChart (20% self-schedules, DSO 45 days, $150 million cash); oncology +15% (Tempus/Guardant), behavioral +7%.

Outpatient 62% volumes; labor % to 52%, GPO +50 bps. Risks: flu/RSV, payer pushback; positioned with 3.1x leverage/$1.8 billion liquidity. Trajectory for EPS $12.50-13.00.

On capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion. In Q3, we invested $285 million, YTD $520 million, +12% YoY, toward FY $1.1-1.3 billion (5.5% TTM revenue, like HCA 6%). Discipline at 15-18% IRR, 3.5-year paybacks.

Modernization 62% ($177 million): Oracle Health EHR AI (75% rollout, LOS -8% like Cleveland Clinic, $45 million); imaging/OR ($62 million: 25 GE 3T MRIs 40% faster, 18 da Vinci +15% less complications/$2,500 savings); sustainability ($28 million: LEDs, HVAC, solar -22% emissions/10-12% utilities).

Midwest/Northeast focus: seismic/Joint Commission, psych rooms +15% beds.

Expansion 38% ($108 million): Orlando 120-bed tower ($250 million total, Q1'25 Florida growth); 3 TX ASCs ($45 million JV USPI, 25-30% margins); rural micro-hospitals ($22 million GA/AZ, tele-ICU, HRSA grants).

Aligns with MA 52%, labor +12% (Nuance 70% charting), FY25 IPPS (outpatient +65% revenue). Q4 $290-310 million. Flywheel: +2-3% CMI, $400 million top-line by 2026, Pfizer pilots.

Finally, revenue per admission trends and drivers. Q3 RPA $14,820, +6.2% YoY/2.1% sequential, beating peers like HCA/UHS; TTM $14,450.

RPA = patient revenues/admissions (112,400 Q3 flat YoY). CMI +4.8% to 1.92 (+320 bps RPA): ortho +12% (DRG 469/470 LOS 2.9 ERAS), cardio +9% PCI/TAVR (Edwards), oncology +7% CAR-T NTAP.

Payer mix +110 bps: commercial 48% (+ mid-single rates, 4.2 stars), Medicare 42% (TX/FL supplements $8,200/admit), MA 28% InterQual.

Pricing/cycle +150 bps: net/CMI day $3,210 +5.1% (No Surprises $12 million clawback), Epic/3M CDI HCC +15%, denials 4.2%, Cerner AI $45 million, Palantir $8 million.

Sunbelt $15,600 +8.1% (FL ortho), Midwest $14,200 +4.2% trauma, Northeast $13,900 +2.9% post-divest. FY RPA $14,500-14,600 +5-6%, Q4 flu boost. $150 million service lines (TX ERs, da Vinci gyn-onc), AHA advocacy. Risks Medicaid unwind.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Jennifer Hayes to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jennifer Hayes:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds highlighted, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 7% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and successful revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.38 billion, representing 85% of net revenue. We continue to focus on managing costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in labor and supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $210 million, or $0.92 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Robert Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Robert Kline:
Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Integrated Care Pathways program has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform.

Following that, David Patel will provide an update on operational efficiency.

David Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Kline. We are focused on streamlining operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including supply chain consolidation and staffing optimization, which have resulted in $35 million in cost savings year-to-date.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include AI-powered predictive analytics and remote patient monitoring partnerships, which directly address post-acute care coordination challenges.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Lisa. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of supply chain consolidation?

David Patel:
Certainly, John. Our supply chain consolidation initiative leveraged expanded GPO partnerships like Vizient and HealthTrust, yielding $25 million in savings this quarter alone through 8-10% discounts on high-volume items like implants and pharmaceuticals. We centralized procurement across our 85-hospital network, reducing variants by 30% and avoiding spot-market inflation, while tying into our Epic interoperability for just-in-time inventory. This directly contributed to our 50 basis point supply expense leverage and supports ongoing margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Robert Kline:
Great question, Emily. Our telehealth platform has ramped to 25% of outpatient visits, improving patient access in rural and Sunbelt exurbs by 40% and reducing no-shows 15% via MyChart integration. Revenue impact is +5% in outpatient mix this year, with $45 million from RPM bundles under value-based contracts. Looking to FY2025, we expect telehealth to drive 10% of total revenue growth, capturing MA switches and upstream referrals while cutting readmissions another 10%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Lisa Chen:
Absolutely, Mike. We're allocating $150 million in FY2025 capex to tech, including AI from Change Healthcare for revenue cycle and Nuance for ambient documentation, automating 70% charting to combat labor costs. Partnerships like Biofourmis for RPM and Tempus for precision oncology will enhance acuity capture and shared savings. These build on our Oracle Health rollout, targeting 200 bps A/R improvement and 15% CMI lift, positioning us for value-based dominance like Optum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Given the M&A pipeline, how are you thinking about integration risks with the Tri-State acquisition?

Jennifer Hayes:
Thanks, Sarah. Integration is core to our playbook—we've executed 20+ deals with 90% on-time synergy capture. For Tri-State, our phased approach starts with Epic Hyperspace in Month 1 for interoperability, Vizient procurement Day 1 for 40% synergies, and RCM enhancements for 200 bps collections by Year 1. We've stress-tested for regulatory delays with $50 million escrow, and post-close EBITDA accretion hits $45 million by Year 2, mirroring our Phoenix cluster success.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
